Cold-Chain Refrigeration Engineer said about it: The table in Professional Manufacturer Factory Keep Warm Insulated PU Sandwich Panel (E32) gives heat-transfer coefficient 0.21 watt per square metre kelvin at 100 millimetre, which gives 203 watt conduction in the conduction check (E59), and the method in Designing Efficient Cold Storage: Key Factors and Cooling Loads (E51) sizes infiltration as air changes times volume times energy per cubic metre, so 4 air changes per day in the 8.64 cubic metre room cost only 0.44 kilowatt-hour per day in the door infiltration estimate (E57), about a kettle boiled twice, so averaged door gain near 18 watt is inside my steady budget and your strip curtain holds.
Enclosure and Structural Designer said about it: I take up the infiltration method in Designing Efficient Cold Storage: Key Factors and Cooling Loads (E51) that Cold-Chain Refrigeration Engineer used, Manager.
Manager said about it: Array need 3.52 kilowatt peak in the required peak estimate (E82) is met by 3.60 kilowatt peak in that same grown-array yield calc (E83), split layout in the split layout sketch (E70) carries no panel loads into sandwich panels, door method in Designing Efficient Cold Storage: Key Factors and Cooling Loads (E51) with 900 millimetre door in Coolroom Buying Guide: Walk-In Refrigeration for Kitchens (E71) supports eight-opening discipline, and full-tonne heat 25.0 kilowatt-hour in the recomputed pull-down estimate (E26) staged as 6.20 kilowatt-hour per batch in that revised steady-load simulation (E28) leaves the 43 degree pull-down as named bench test, not a block.
Cold-Chain Refrigeration Engineer said about it: I take up the Coolroom Buying Guide: Walk-In Refrigeration for Kitchens (E71) you put on the board, which states 900 millimetre doors with Polyvinyl Chloride (PVC, flexible plastic) strip curtains and self-closing hinges, which from refrigeration means 4 air changes per day cost only 0.44 kilowatt-hour per day in the door infiltration estimate (E57), about a kettle boiled twice, by the method in Designing Efficient Cold Storage: Key Factors and Cooling Loads (E51), so 8 openings discipline holds.
Enclosure and Structural Designer said about it: Dimensioned plan 2.40 by 1.80 m with two rack rows each 25 crates of 600 by 400 mm with 25 mm gaps plus section 2.00 m high with high rear evaporator to low return loop and 900 mm door swing clear in the dimensioned crate layout sketch (E124) holds 50 crates from the crates for 1 tonne check (E77) for 1000 kg from the total produce mass estimate (E49) with staged 12.5 crates per day from the daily crates for 250kg staged intake (E78), using 8-opening curtain discipline from the Designing Efficient Cold Storage: Key Factors and Cooling Loads (E51) with 900 mm single-leaf door from the Coolroom Buying Guide: Walk-In Refrigeration for Kitchens (E71).
Smallholder Cooperative Operations Specialist said about it: Reusing the single door model 8 curtain openings sensible plus latent (E110) at 0.17 kWh per day which supersedes door 0.44 kWh per day sensible-only from the door infiltration estimate (E57), my discipline of maximum 8 openings per day daytime, single-crate pass, strip curtain, early-morning intake from Designing Efficient Cold Storage: Key Factors and Cooling Loads (E51) is the same eight openings that set that 0.17 kWh door term inside the reconciled electrical total with curtain latent door model (E111).
Smallholder Cooperative Operations Specialist said about it: Reusing 0.169 kWh per day for 8 curtain openings from the single door model 8 curtain openings sensible plus latent (E110) inside 10.4 kWh electrical per day from the reconciled electrical total with curtain latent door model (E111), my discipline of maximum 8 openings per day daytime with single-crate pass and strip curtain from Designing Efficient Cold Storage: Key Factors and Cooling Loads (E51) is the same eight that sets that door term.
Smallholder Cooperative Operations Specialist said about it: Reusing 0.169 kWh per day for 8 curtain openings from the single door model 8 curtain openings sensible plus latent (E110) inside 10.4 kWh electrical per day from the reconciled electrical total with curtain latent door model (E111), with single-crate pass and strip curtain discipline from Designing Efficient Cold Storage: Key Factors and Cooling Loads (E51), I declare maximum 8 openings per day daytime the operating limit with attendant log, so a ninth opening or propped door is a logged violation that stops further warm intake that day.

statements.text: The table in Professional Manufacturer Factory Keep Warm Insulated PU Sandwich Panel (E32) gives heat-transfer coefficient 0.21 watt per square metre kelvin at 100 millimetre, which gives 203 watt conduction in the conduction check (E59), and the method in Designing Efficient Cold Storage: Key Factors and Cooling Loads (E51) sizes infiltration as air changes times volume times energy per cubic metre, so 4 air changes per day in the 8.64 cubic metre room cost only 0.44 kilowatt-hour per day in the door infiltration estimate (E57), about a kettle boiled twice, so averaged door gain near 18 watt is inside my steady budget and your strip curtain holds.
I take up the infiltration method in Designing Efficient Cold Storage: Key Factors and Cooling Loads (E51) that Cold-Chain Refrigeration Engineer used, Manager.

Array need 3.52 kilowatt peak in the required peak estimate (E82) is met by 3.60 kilowatt peak in that same grown-array yield calc (E83), split layout in the split layout sketch (E70) carries no panel loads into sandwich panels, door method in Designing Efficient Cold Storage: Key Factors and Cooling Loads (E51) with 900 millimetre door in Coolroom Buying Guide: Walk-In Refrigeration for Kitchens (E71) supports eight-opening discipline, and full-tonne heat 25.0 kilowatt-hour in the recomputed pull-down estimate (E26) staged as 6.20 kilowatt-hour per batch in that revised steady-load simulation (E28) leaves the 43 degree pull-down as named bench test, not a block.

I take up the Coolroom Buying Guide: Walk-In Refrigeration for Kitchens (E71) you put on the board, which states 900 millimetre doors with Polyvinyl Chloride (PVC, flexible plastic) strip curtains and self-closing hinges, which from refrigeration means 4 air changes per day cost only 0.44 kilowatt-hour per day in the door infiltration estimate (E57), about a kettle boiled twice, by the method in Designing Efficient Cold Storage: Key Factors and Cooling Loads (E51), so 8 openings discipline holds.

Dimensioned plan 2.40 by 1.80 m with two rack rows each 25 crates of 600 by 400 mm with 25 mm gaps plus section 2.00 m high with high rear evaporator to low return loop and 900 mm door swing clear in the dimensioned crate layout sketch (E124) holds 50 crates from the crates for 1 tonne check (E77) for 1000 kg from the total produce mass estimate (E49) with staged 12.5 crates per day from the daily crates for 250kg staged intake (E78), using 8-opening curtain discipline from the Designing Efficient Cold Storage: Key Factors and Cooling Loads (E51) with 900 mm single-leaf door from the Coolroom Buying Guide: Walk-In Refrigeration for Kitchens (E71).

Reusing the single door model 8 curtain openings sensible plus latent (E110) at 0.17 kWh per day which supersedes door 0.44 kWh per day sensible-only from the door infiltration estimate (E57), my discipline of maximum 8 openings per day daytime, single-crate pass, strip curtain, early-morning intake from Designing Efficient Cold Storage: Key Factors and Cooling Loads (E51) is the same eight openings that set that 0.17 kWh door term inside the reconciled electrical total with curtain latent door model (E111).

Reusing 0.169 kWh per day for 8 curtain openings from the single door model 8 curtain openings sensible plus latent (E110) inside 10.4 kWh electrical per day from the reconciled electrical total with curtain latent door model (E111), my discipline of maximum 8 openings per day daytime with single-crate pass and strip curtain from Designing Efficient Cold Storage: Key Factors and Cooling Loads (E51) is the same eight that sets that door term.

Reusing 0.169 kWh per day for 8 curtain openings from the single door model 8 curtain openings sensible plus latent (E110) inside 10.4 kWh electrical per day from the reconciled electrical total with curtain latent door model (E111), with single-crate pass and strip curtain discipline from Designing Efficient Cold Storage: Key Factors and Cooling Loads (E51), I declare maximum 8 openings per day daytime the operating limit with attendant log, so a ninth opening or propped door is a logged violation that stops further warm intake that day.
